messages:
maria g: Alert from monitoring — nvml Xid spikes on us-west2 A10 pool, ~30 total in last 5m (mix of Xid13/Xid31). Some pods saw instant OOMs and retries.

infra-bot: [auto-alert] nvml_xid_errors_total > threshold (region=us-west-2, gpu_type=a10). Created incident: INC-176789.

aj chen: on it. which node ids? any ECC counts?

maria g: node list from telemetry: a10-usw2-n0{node-7f2}, a10-usw2-n3{node-c1b}. quick excerpt from driver logs:
```
[2026-03-10T21:04:12Z] NVML: Xid 31: GPU fault detected, process 4321 (python) batch=2048
[2026-03-10T21:04:14Z] NVML: Xid 13: GPU exception during kernel launch
[2026-03-10T21:04:15Z] ECC correctable count: +2
```

liam: I ran a quick query against our metrics to group by xid:
```
sum by (xid) (increase(nvidia_xid_errors_total{region="us-west-2",gpu_type="a10"}[5m]))
```
result: Xid31=18, Xid13=9, Xid48=2. timeline aligns with heavy traffic from search-embedder.

sophia: checking ECC uncorrectable:
```
sum(increase(nvidia_ecc_uncorrectable_total{region="us-west-2",gpu_type="a10"}[1h]))
```
--> 0 on those hosts (good), only correctables bumped. suggests transient kernel/driver faults not raw memory kills.

aj chen: interesting — embedder workload uses int8 quantized kernels and larger batch sizes. can we correlate per-tenant request rate with Xid spikes?

maria g: yes, matched tenant tags: search-embedder-svc traffic jumped +3x at 21:02 and coincides with Xid burst. attaching sample pod logs (short):
```
/opt/venv/bin/python -m embedder.server serve --batch 2048 --quant=int8
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../inference/ops.cu", line 412, in forward
NVML: Xid 31
```

liam: repro plan: throttle embedder to batch=512 on a canary node and run the same request ramp, see if Xid reproduces. if it does, likely kernel/launch contention or thermal/driver race at high batch sizes.

sophia: also worth testing latest driver on a staging A10 (we're on 525.85 currently). there are a couple of driver fixes for kernel launch races in the 525.x -> 530.x series.

aj chen: operational options:
- isolate offending pods (taint + nodeSelector)
- repro with smaller batchsize and new driver on staging
- if NVML persists, drain node and mark for replacement (possible flaky card)

kubectl command to cordon+drain:
```
kubectl cordon a10-usw2-n3
kubectl drain a10-usw2-n3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria g: agree. cost/avail note: draining two A10 nodes reduces pool throughput by ~18%. we should shift embedder traffic to us-east-1 as fallback while we triage to avoid customer impact.

liam: putting repro job on a staging A10 with driver 530.41 + batch=2048, will post results in 30m. if we see reproduction, we escalate to vendor RMA for that GPU.

sophia: also added a short-term mitigation in routing: per-tenant rate limiter for search-embedder to cap burst concurrency to 60. should cut worst-case pressure.

aj chen: I'll open hardware ticket and schedule replacement for node-c1b if failures continue after driver bump. RMA draft ID: RMA-2026-132.

maria g: plan for tonight 02:00 UTC window: drain a10-usw2-n3, repro on staging, upgrade driver on canary, monitor for 2h. notify support & affected tenants.

infra-bot: Updated incident INC-176789: runbook link https://redwood-internal/runbooks/xid-triage, postmortem template created.

maria g: thanks — tagging @aj chen and @liam. anyone else see different signal?

aj chen: noted. I'll coordinate fallback routing + hardware ops.

liam: repro started, will update.

sophia: monitoring dashboards: added a per-xid heatmap and tenant overlap panel. will keep an eye.
